chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Fadhl from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: In the case of a man who freed his slave while death was approaching him, and he testified to that, and the slave's value was six hundred dirhams, and he had a debt of three hundred dirhams, and he left nothing else, he said: 'One-sixth of him is freed, because he only has three hundred from him, and he has one-sixth of the total.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on manumitting a slave while in the deathbed state regarding debt and estate division?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the scholar clarifies the calculation of manumission costs during the final illness (marad al-mawt) by treating the slave's value as a debt against the estate. The ruling specifies that one-sixth of the slave's assessed value (six hundred dirhams) is allocated to cover the debt, demonstrating the principle that manumission expenses are prioritized similarly to other financial obligations before the distribution of the remaining inheritance.
